newsitem.title: UK: Leasing expanding rapidly in emerging markets - IFC.
newsitem.headline: Leasing expanding rapidly in emerging markets - IFC.

text.p: Leasing has become a major industry in emerging markets, growing from around $15 billion in 1988 to $44 billion in 1994, and is set to grow further, a report from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) said.

The Washington-based IFC said leasing, whereby a lessee uses an asset and pays rental on it to a lessor who owns the asset, was a mature industry in most high-income economies. But by 1994, the latest year for which global data is available, middle and low income countries accounted for five out of the 20 largest leasing markets.
The IFC said the most spectacular increase had been in South Korea, which started leasing in 1975 and by 1994 was the world's fifth largest market.
Market penetration (leasing as share of private investment) more than doubled in both low and middle income countries between 1988 and 1994, the report, released this week said.
Leasing arrangements now account for 11 percent of the financing of capital equipment in middle income countries, up from just four percent in 1988.
The IFC said cross country comparisons were difficult because of different regulatory and fiscal environments.

But in 1994 Asia accounted for 28 percent of the world leasing market, having overtaken Europe in 1993, which had 25 percent of market share. Latin's America's share increased fivefold to 4.2 percent in 1994 from 0.8 percent in 1989.

The IFC said Africa's share had also grown to 1.3 percent of the global total, but it was made up mainly by South Africa and Morocco, which had both been among the top 50 leasing markets every year since 1989.

The IFC said it would continue to promote leasing because it benefited small and medium sized companies in developing countries and worked "even in risky countries with poor access to international capital".
The arrangement had also "addressed an important unmet demand and attracted borrowers away from tradiitonal financial products such as bank loans", it said.

The report said the IFC will advise governments, locate international technical partners, invest in new leasing companies, help leasing companies raise finance, promote cross-border leasing and "big-ticket" leasing for sectors such as infrastructure, among other measures.
